extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in natural science and scientific biography
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluative principles and disciplinary standards embedded in a Popular Science Monthly issue containing natural-history exposition, experimental physiology (symbiosis), and a scientific biography/essay on methodology and education. The page presents methodological norms, criteria for biological identification, and competing standards for literary vs. scientific education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation and experimentation as the foundations of scientific medicine
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation and experiments only have a permanent value; both facts and experimentation are the only admissible foundations of scientific medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virchow argues against speculative, a priori systems not founded on facts or experimentation. He advocates collecting material honestly and giving credit where due; patience in collecting facts even if it takes long; pathological physiology should grow out of observation and experiment and will form the fortress of scientific medicine, with pathological anatomy and clinical research as outworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular localization of disease (cellular pathology)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cellular pathology the localization of disease is a necessity — the seat of disease is fixed in the smallest composing element, the cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virchow's criterion holds that disease results from disorder/changes within cells; external causes act by producing mechanical or chemical changes within cells. Predisposition depends on the condition of different cells. This view implies therapeutics become more exact and local in application, and that many pathological facts find explanation within the cellular framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for identifying green bodies in animals as independent algae (zoochlorella/zooxanthella)
rubrics_metrics.description: Morphological and physiological independence indicate that the green/yellow bodies in animals are one-celled algae (zoochlorella/zooxanthella) rather than self-formed chlorophyl of the animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphological evidence: green bodies are not uniformly green, contain colorless protoplasm or a distinguishable cell-kernel, and show signs of division (cell-kernels) — unlike normal plant chlorophyl-cells which lack a cell-kernel. Physiological evidence: when separated from hosts these bodies survive for days/weeks, form starch in sunlight, and when grafted onto chlorophyl-free hydras or infusoria they continue to live, demonstrating independence and capacity to perform photosynthetic assimilation that can sustain the host. Experimental protocols (extraction, microscopy, grafting, cultivation in filtered water) are cited as methods to establish independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational standard: teach established facts/results, not unestablished theories, in public schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Only established facts and results, not theories, should be taught in the public schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virchow, while not opposed to Darwinism per se, objects to Haeckel's insistence that theories like natural selection be included in elementary public education; he draws a boundary between science (which should teach established knowledge) and faith/theory (which lies beyond that boundary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary-education criterion: 'know the best that has been thought and said'
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of literary culture is to know the best that has been thought and said in the world — i.e., the choicest, finest, most excellent literary performances (classical and modern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arnold's position frames literary education around mastery of canonical works (Greek, Roman, Eastern antiquity and one another) and interprets 'best' as the supreme literary performances. This serves as a standard for curricular content and for judging the quality of literary cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-educational criterion: include physical science in the common intellectual 'outfit'
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation's or individual's intellectual/spiritual progress requires drawing from the stores of physical science; lacking knowledge of recent physical-science advances weakens the capacity to critique life or culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in contrast to Arnold's literary-only programme (quoted from Huxley): intellectual progress needs an acquaintance with physical science as part of the common educational equipment; metaphorical guidance (army without precision weapons) is used to argue that omission of science handicaps effective criticism and advancement.
